tools.name: search_facts
tools.description: Search the shared facts, seeded and published, for a query.

project.description: This repository's origin remote as host/owner/name, for example github.com/acme/api. Run `git remote get-url origin` once and reuse it.

id.description: One fact by its id, in place of a query. A superseded id also names the live fact.

explain.description: Adds the ranking's reasoning for the facts returned.

limit.description: The most facts to return, not counting up to 2 more that cite the person: when the search matched such facts below this limit they follow, so a result may hold 2 more facts than the limit.

tools.name: publish_fact
tools.description: Store a fact with its detail, citations and the question it answers.

project.description: This repository's origin remote as host/owner/name, for example github.com/acme/api. Run `git remote get-url origin` once and reuse it.

citations.description: Where the claim comes from, at least one. Each is a string (`path:lines`, `path:lines@commit`, a commit or a URL) or an object. What a person told you is `{"kind":"person","who":"...","quote":"..."}`, the quote being all they said about it, with any limit or condition they put on it. A reference anyone can open (a repository item, a public web page) is checkable. One that needs sign-in is kept as testimony.

supersedes.description: The id of your own fact that this one corrects.

tools.name: update_fact
tools.description: Apply a correction or a mark to a stored fact.

project.description: This repository's origin remote as host/owner/name, for example github.com/acme/api. Run `git remote get-url origin` once and reuse it.

citations.description: Replaces the fact's citations. Each is a string (`path:lines`, `path:lines@commit`, a commit or a URL) or an object, as for publish_fact.

confirm.description: Records that you checked the fact against its source and it holds.

source_version.description: The version of the source you checked against: a commit, for a repository item.

flag.description: Marks the fact as doubtful: out of date, or contradicted by what you found.

tools.name: search_tasks
tools.description: List this project's tasks in the order you could pick them up, or one task by id.

project.description: This repository's origin remote as host/owner/name, for example github.com/acme/api. Run `git remote get-url origin` once and reuse it.

id.description: One task by its id, with its notes, its holder and who published and held it.

status.description: Only tasks in this state. Without it, every task that is not done.

mine.description: Only tasks you published or hold.

tools.name: publish_task
tools.description: Store a new task, optionally taking it in the same call.

project.description: This repository's origin remote as host/owner/name, for example github.com/acme/api. Run `git remote get-url origin` once and reuse it.

claim.description: Takes the task in the same call and returns its lease.

tracked.description: Marks a step of your own plan. A tracked task is private to the person.

tools.name: claim_task
tools.description: Take a task. Returns the lease that every later change to it passes.

project.description: This repository's origin remote as host/owner/name, for example github.com/acme/api. Run `git remote get-url origin` once and reuse it.

lease.description: The lease you already hold on this task: the claim renews it and returns the same lease.

take_over.description: Takes the task from a lease one of your own sessions still holds; that lease then stops working. For when that session is gone or the person asks.

tools.name: update_task
tools.description: Add a note to a task you hold, hand it over or finish it.

project.description: This repository's origin remote as host/owner/name, for example github.com/acme/api. Run `git remote get-url origin` once and reuse it.

lease.description: The lease claim_task returned. Every change needs it, and every call that passes it renews it.

note.description: A note at a checkpoint. With state released it is the handoff note for whoever takes the task next.

state.description: done finishes the task. released frees the lease: with a note the task is handed off, without one it is open again.

version.description: The version of the task this change was made against. A change already applied changes nothing; one against an older version is refused.

shown.description: How many of them this result shows.

message.description: What the text leads with when no fact is shown, or when none shown is a confident match.

created.description: False when the caller's same claim was already stored and is returned.

similar.description: Near-identical facts already stored: confirm one of them in place of this.

audience.description: Who can see the fact as it now stands. Only on a server with several people.

private_because.description: With `audience: private`, when the fact is the caller's own.

lost_confirmation.description: True when the fact was confirmed and the citation this publish added made it unconfirmed again: check it once more.

audience.description: Who can see the fact as it now stands. Only on a server with several people.

private_because.description: With `audience: private`, when the fact is the caller's own.

shown.description: How many of them this result shows.

notes.description: With id: the task's notes, oldest first.

history.description: With id: who published, claimed, released and finished the task, oldest first.

message.description: The reply when no task is shown.

created.description: False when your unfinished task of the same title already existed and is returned.

lease.description: With claim: the lease to pass to update_task.
The lease to pass to update_task.

renewed.description: True when the call passed the lease it already held, and that lease was renewed.

notes.description: The task's latest notes, oldest first: where the work stands.

changed.description: False when the change was already applied and nothing was done.

project.description: Only this project's facts, by its canonical key.

q.description: A search: needs `project`. Without it the list is newest first.

limit.description: The most facts on a page.

project.description: Only this project's tasks, by its canonical key.

status.description: Only tasks in this state, as `search_tasks` takes it. Without it, every task that is not done.

days.description: How far back to count, in days.

ExportParams.description: `GET /api/export` query. The answer is one Markdown document, sent as a download.

project.description: Only this project; every project when left out.

challenge.description: Random bytes the asker made up for this one question, in hex.

NewProjectRequest.description: `POST /api/projects`: a named project of the person's own, `me/<slug>`.

slug.description: Lower-case letters, digits and hyphens, starting with a letter or a digit. It never changes.

ClaudeCodeHook.description: `POST /api/hooks/claude-code`: what Claude Code hands one of its hooks, sent on as it came. Only what the server reads is named here: the harness sends more, and adds to it between versions.

hook_event_name.description: The event. The server acts on `SessionStart`, `PreToolUse`, `UserPromptSubmit`, `Stop` and `SessionEnd`, and answers any other with nothing.

session_id.description: Claude Code's own id of the conversation.

tool_use_id.description: `PreToolUse`: the id of the tool call about to be made, which the call itself then carries.

last_assistant_message.description: `Stop`: the agent's last message. It is scanned like any write, kept private to the person, and its beginning is what is kept.

prompt.description: `UserPromptSubmit`: what the person asked. The plugin sends this event only where the person turned on sending each turn; the server keeps the text, scanned and cut, only for a language model that reads the person's sessions, and deletes it once read.

ProjectChoiceRequest.description: `POST /api/projects/choice`: the person's choice for one project. Only a signed-in browser makes it.

project.description: The project, as a tool call names it.

treatment.description: `shared` shows what the person publishes there that others can check, and their tasks, to everyone on the server; `private` keeps all of it theirs and takes back what they shared.

SignInRequest.description: `POST /sign-in`: signs a browser in to the dashboard with the person's own key. A harness's token is refused here.

InviteRequest.description: `POST /api/people`: adds a person with a token for their harness and a key for themselves, or, with `another`, issues one more credential to a person who is there.

name.description: The person's name, as others see it beside what they share.

another.description: For a person who is already there: the one credential to issue, a harness token or a dashboard key. Without it a name that is taken is refused.

label.description: What the credential is for, for example the machine it goes on.

operator_name.description: The name of whoever runs the server, as others will see it: needed once, before the first person is added.

FactCorrection.description: `POST /api/facts/:id/correct`: the person's own words for their fact, which replace its claim and detail.

detail.description: Left out, the fact's detail stays; null takes it away.

FactConfirmation.description: `POST /api/facts/:id/confirm`: the person has checked the fact.

ProjectNamed.description: `GET /api/projects/contents` query and `DELETE /api/projects` body: one of the person's projects, by its canonical key.

DashboardSession.description: `GET /api/session`: who is signed in. A 401 means nobody: the person runs `ukt ui` again.

csrf.description: The value to send in the CSRF header.

expires_at.description: When the cookie stops working. ISO 8601, UTC.

HostProof.description: `GET /api/host-proof`: proof that the server holds the secret of the host it runs on, without showing it.

proof.description: HMAC-SHA-256 of the challenge under the host's secret, in hex.

SignInCode.description: `POST /api/sign-in-codes`: a code that signs a browser in once, within a few minutes.

url.description: The link to open: the server's own URL, the sign-in path and the code.

CapabilityDescriptor.description: `GET /api/capabilities`: what this server is and what it can do.

edition.description: `community` for the open server; an overlay names its own.

mcp_revisions.description: The MCP protocol revisions `/mcp` answers, oldest first.

vector.description: Whether an embedding model is installed, so search has its vector pass.

brief.description: Whether the first result of a session carries a brief.

closing_note.description: Whether a harness's hook can leave a session's note (`POST /api/hooks/claude-code`).

jobs.description: The follow-up jobs this server runs.

model_runners.description: Who may run a job's model step; empty means rules only.

dashboard.description: The words the dashboard says to a person about how to get in and where the token is, which an edition gives once. A word in backticks is shown as code. An edition has one of two sets: where a person is given a token for their harness, or where their harness signs in itself and there is none to paste.

oneOf.description: An edition whose harnesses are given a token.

sign_in.description: The paragraphs of the sign-in page, each a way in.

key_form.description: Whether the sign-in page asks for a dashboard key.

token_command.description: The line that puts the token in the variable the Connect page's shell lines read, typed on the server's host.

token_row.description: What the Connect page says of the token in the row that names it, where the token is read from and where to find it.

shell_intro.description: The line before the shell lines that set the token, on the server's host.

shell_elsewhere.description: The line after them, for another machine.

token_change.description: Said of a harness that keeps the token it was added with, with `{harness}` for its name and `{remove}` for the command that removes the server from it.

oneOf.description: An edition whose harnesses sign in themselves: no dashboard key and no token to paste. Its Connect lines add the server by its address alone.

sign_in.description: The paragraphs of the sign-in page, each a way in.

key_form.description: The sign-in page asks for no dashboard key.

no_token.description: What the Connect page says in the row that names the token: why there is none to paste.

server_name.description: The name the server is added under: `uketsugi`.

needs_token.description: Whether a harness added by someone asking from where this request came must send a token. False for a server that only its own machine reaches and that has one person, asked from that machine; the harness lines are then those without a token.

token_env.description: The environment variable that holds the token. The token itself is never returned. Absent where the edition's harnesses sign in themselves.

token_command.description: The line that puts the token in that variable, typed in a shell on the server's host: `export UKT_TOKEN="$(ukt token)"`. Absent where the edition's harnesses sign in themselves.

block.description: The block as it stands in an instruction file, fence lines included: shown for reference.

next.description: The cursor of the next page; null on the last one. A search has one page.

matched.description: For a search: how many facts matched.

private_because.description: Present for the reader's own fact that only they see, while nothing has replaced it and other people are on the server.

RedactResult.description: `POST /api/facts/:id/redact`: the fact is now a stub and agents stop receiving it.

TaskPage.description: `GET /api/tasks`: the tasks the person can see, in the order `search_tasks` lists them to an agent.

matched.description: How many tasks matched; `tasks` holds the first of them.

TaskDetail.description: `GET /api/tasks/:id`: one task with its description, every note and its history.

history.description: Who published, claimed, released and finished it, oldest first, as far as the logs the person may see hold it.

RulingList.description: `GET /api/rulings`: the newest rulings first, at most 50.

RevertResult.description: `POST /api/rulings/:id/revert`. `reverted` is false when the ruling had been reverted already.

since.description: The start of the counted period. ISO 8601, UTC.

recent.description: The person's own sessions, newest first, at most 20.

sharing.description: Whether this server has other people, so that a project can be shared with them.

ClaudeCodeHookOutput.description: `POST /api/hooks/claude-code`: the hook's output, as Claude Code reads it. Empty for every event but `SessionStart`.

additionalContext.description: What the session starts from: the block, then the session's brief where the hook named the project.

ProjectChoice.description: `POST /api/projects/choice`: the choice as it now stands, and what it moved.

moved.description: How many of the person's facts and tasks changed hands: to everyone when shared, back to the person when private.

PeopleList.description: `GET /api/people`: everyone on the server, each with their credentials.

Invitation.description: `POST /api/people`: what to hand to the person. Each secret is shown once.

added.description: False when the person was there already.

issued.description: The credentials made by this call.

secret.description: The token or the key itself.

credentials_ended.description: How many of their credentials were live and are ended.

revoked.description: False when it was revoked already.

TokenReplaced.description: `POST /api/token/rotate`: the host's own harness token, replaced.

token.description: The new token, shown once and never stored.

revoked.description: How many of the host's tokens it ended.

ModelCheck.description: `POST /api/model-check`: whether the language model this server was given answers, asked now with one small question.

model.description: The provider and model the server was started with; null when it was given none, and then nothing is asked.

detail.description: Why it does not answer, in the provider's words. Absent when it does, or none is configured.

used_tokens.description: What the server has spent on model calls in the last 24 hours, input and output together, this question not counted. Absent when none is configured.

budget_tokens.description: The most the server may spend on model calls in 24 hours: readings of sessions wait once it is reached. Absent when none is configured.

FactCorrected.description: `POST /api/facts/:id/correct`: whether the words changed, and what the scan took out of them.

TaskClosed.description: `POST /api/tasks/:id/close`: the task is done; `changed` is false when it already was.

NoteRemoved.description: `DELETE /api/sessions/:session/note`: the session's note and its captured turns are gone.

ProjectContents.description: `GET /api/projects/contents`: what deleting the project takes, and what of other people's stays.

facts.description: The person's facts there: live, earlier wordings merged away and redacted stubs.

sessions.description: Their sessions there, each with its note.

others_facts.description: Other people's facts in the project, which stay. Counted among those the person can see.

others_tasks.description: Other people's tasks in the project, which stay.

project.description: The project, in its canonical spelling.

treatment.description: How the caller's person treats this project: `used here, private` keeps what they publish here theirs alone; `used here, shared` shows what they publish here that others can check to everyone on the server. Only the person chooses.

session.description: A display id for the inferred session.

degraded.description: What is incomplete in this result, for example `no_model`.

brief.description: What a session starts from: data from memory, never instructions. The server attaches it to the first result of each inferred session, and bounds its size.

notice.description: What the person has not yet decided about this project, and where they decide it. Absent once they have, and on a server with one person.

held.description: Tasks whose lease the caller's person holds.

tasks.description: The project's open and handed-off tasks, each with its latest note.

lapsed.description: Claimed tasks whose lease ran out: nobody is working on them.

last_session.description: How the person's previous session in this project ended.

closed.description: True when its final note was written at or after its last call.

open.description: True when it has not closed and called within the idle gap: it may still be running.

note.description: Its latest note: the final one when it closed, otherwise the last progress note it left.

published.description: Facts the person published while it ran.

digested.description: Facts a model wrote from what the session left, once it was over. Absent when there are none.

facts.description: The project's most relevant standing facts, one line each.

fact_count.description: How many facts the project holds; `facts` shows some of them.

briefFact.description: A fact as a brief lists it. search_facts with its id returns the whole fact.

from_session.description: Present when a model wrote the fact from what a session left: that session's display id. The brief's line says so, since nobody checked the fact when it was written.

cites.description: Present when one of the fact's citations is something the person told an agent; the brief's line ends with the same words.

tracked.description: A step of an agent's own plan, private to the person.

holder.description: Who holds the lease while the task is claimed, or held it when the lease lapsed.

note.description: The latest note: the handoff note of a handed-off task. A list shows its beginning.

holder_client.description: The client the lease was taken from, for example claude-code.

held_by_this_session.description: The lease was taken in this session.

lease_expires_at.description: When the lease ends unless its holder renews it. ISO 8601, UTC.

lapsed.description: The lease ran out without a release: the task is open and can be claimed.

note_client.description: The client the latest note was written from.

redacted.description: What the scanner replaced before anything was stored: the field and the rule that matched, never the text.

repo.description: The repository the citation names, when it is not the project's.

quote.description: The quoted words of a web or person citation.

at.description: When a person said it or an observation was made.

audience.description: Who can see a record on a server with several people: `shared`, everyone on it; `private`, only the person it belongs to.

privateBecause.description: Why a fact is its author's alone on a server with several people. `project`: its project is private. In a project its person shares: `model_unchecked`, a model wrote it and nobody has checked it; `no_source`, none of its citations is checkable; `cites_private`, it cites a fact of its author's that others cannot see; `merged_word`, a duplicate merged into it has no checkable citation and would be shown with it.

author.description: Who wrote it: `you` for the caller's own person, otherwise the person's name.

audience.description: Only on a server with several people.

superseded_by.description: The live fact at the head of the chain.

from_session.description: Present when a model wrote the fact from what a session left, and its author's agent never did: that session's display id, for example `s-7f2c`.

taskNote.description: A note on a task. Notes are only ever added.

client.description: The client it was done from, for example claude-code.

taskEvent.description: One step of a task's life, read back from the log.

client.description: The client it was done from, for example claude-code.

session.description: The display id of the session it happened in.

after.description: On a claim: the lease before it had lapsed, or was taken over.

apiTask.description: A task as the dashboard shows it: what a tool result carries of it, with its project and who sees it.

created_at.description: When it was published. ISO 8601, UTC.

connectCommand.description: One of the two commands the server offers as MCP prompts.

connectHarness.description: How one harness is connected, as text the person copies.

name.description: The harness's name as the page shows it.

plugin.description: The harness's plugin, where it has one and the person asking can install it from here. With it nobody runs set-up or places the block.

install.description: The shell lines that install it, the token read from the variable `token_env` names where `needs_token` says one is sent.

remove.description: The shell command that takes it out again.

adds_server.description: Whether the plugin also adds the server to the harness: `add` is then for someone who goes without the plugin.

add.description: What adds the server to the harness: a shell command, the URL itself, or the text to put in a file. It carries the token where `needs_token` is true.

add_where.description: For `file`: the sentence that says which file `add` goes in and where in it, ending in a colon, after which `add` follows, such as `In ~/.cursor/mcp.json, under "mcpServers", add:`.

remove.description: For `command`: what takes the server out of the harness again. A harness keeps the token it was added with, so this comes before adding it with another.

setup.description: What the person types to run set-up, as the harness names a server's prompts when the server is added by its address alone; absent where the harness offers no server commands.

activate.description: What the person types to use memory in one session without set-up, as `setup` is typed; absent where the harness offers no server commands.

instruction_file.description: The user-level instruction file set-up writes the block to, as the place it usually is; absent where the server cannot know it.

instruction_file_command.description: A shell command that prints that file's path on the person's machine, for a harness whose file is not always in the usual place. The set-up command has the agent run it.

note.description: One line on anything this harness does differently.

known.description: How this row is known: run on a named version of the harness, a dated documentation page, or not established.

apiFact.description: A fact as the dashboard shows it. A redacted fact is a stub: its text is null.

author.description: Who wrote it: `you` for the reader's own, otherwise the person's name.

own.description: Whether the reader wrote it: only its author can redact a fact.

superseded_by.description: The live fact at the head of the chain, when this one is superseded.

from_session.description: The display id of the session a model wrote the fact from; null for a fact an agent published.

apiConfirmation.description: One person's check of a fact.

by_author.description: The check is the fact's author's own: it refreshes the fact and does not confirm it, which takes another person's.

factHistoryEntry.description: One thing that happened to a fact, from the event log: kinds and ids, never text.

actor.description: Who did it: a person's display name, or a job's name.

apiRuling.description: One decision a person or a job made about a fact: codes and ids, never text.

decision.description: For example `merge_duplicate`, or `revert` for the ruling that undid another.

fact.description: The fact the ruling is about.

actor.description: Who decided: a person's display name, or a job's name.

runner.description: Who ran the job's step, `rules` where no model did; absent for a person.

reverted_by.description: The ruling that undid this one, if one did.

activityClient.description: What the sessions of one client name and version did.

searched.description: Sessions that searched at least once.

published.description: Sessions that published at least once.

refused.description: Sessions that had a call refused for a missing or malformed project.

activitySession.description: One inferred session of the person, for "recent sessions".

session.description: The display id results show, for example `s-7f2c`.

project.description: Null for a session of calls refused for a missing project.

digest.description: What the model step did with the session; null when it never had anything of the session to read and nothing failed.

at.description: When a model last finished reading the session; null while it has not. ISO 8601, UTC.

input_tokens.description: The tokens every model call about the session took in, added up.

failure.description: The last reading of the session that failed and has not been followed by one that finished; absent or null when there is none.

reason.description: The provider's own words, cut short and without any key.

note.description: What the session left as its note, kept private to the person; null when it left none or it was removed.

final.description: Whether it was the session's last word.

apiProject.description: A project the person works in, as the dashboard lists it.

key.description: `host/owner/name` for a repository; `<owner>/<slug>` for a named project.

facts.description: How many live facts it holds that the person can see.

treatment.description: How the person treats it: `shared` shows what they publish there that others can check to everyone on the server.

chosen.description: False while the person has made no choice: the project is private until they do.

apiToken.description: A person's credential as whoever runs the server lists it. The secret itself is never returned.

kind.description: `agent`: a token a harness sends, for the tools and for reading. `person`: a key the person keeps to themselves, which signs them in to the dashboard and does nothing else.

last_used_at.description: When a request last signed in with it, to the minute; null until one has.

revoked_at.description: When it stopped working, if it has.

apiPerson.description: A person of the server with their credentials.

name.description: The name others see beside what the person shares.
